name: Advent: waiting for the King
summary: Seven promises of the coming King and how they came true in Jesus.

steps.title: The first promise
steps.note: At the very start of the story, God promises a child who will defeat evil. Paul says Jesus came at exactly the right time, born of a woman.
steps.question: Why do you think God made this promise so soon after things went wrong?

steps.title: A king from David's family
steps.note: God promises David a son whose kingdom will last. Gabriel tells Mary her son will receive David's throne.
steps.question: What kind of king were people expecting, and what kind of king did Jesus turn out to be?

steps.title: God with us
steps.note: Isaiah gives a sign of a child called Immanuel. Matthew sees its full meaning in Jesus, God with us.
steps.question: What difference does it make that God came to be with us, not just to help from a distance?

steps.title: A child is born
steps.note: Isaiah announces a child with names like Wonderful Counselor and Prince of Peace. The angels announce the Savior born in Bethlehem.
steps.question: Which of Isaiah's names for this child means the most to you right now?

steps.title: Prepare the way
steps.note: A voice calls for a road to be made ready for God. John the Baptist is that voice, preparing people for Jesus.
steps.question: What would preparing the way for Jesus look like in your life this Advent?

steps.title: Little Bethlehem
steps.note: God chooses a small town for the birth of a great ruler. The scholars point Herod to Micah's words.
steps.question: Why might God choose small and humble places to do great things?

steps.title: The sunrise
steps.note: The last Old Testament prophet pictures the sun of righteousness rising with healing. Zechariah sings that this sunrise has come.
steps.question: Where do you need God's light and healing as you wait for Christmas?

name: Christmas: the Word became flesh
summary: Why the birth of Jesus matters, from creation to the wise men.

steps.title: In the beginning
steps.note: John begins his Gospel with the same words as Genesis. The one born at Christmas was there at creation.
steps.question: How does it change your view of Christmas that the baby in the manger is the Word who made the world?

steps.title: The Word became flesh
steps.note: Paul describes Christ choosing to become a servant and be born as a man. John says the Word made his home among us.
steps.question: What does it tell you about God that he came in such a humble way?

steps.title: A great light
steps.note: People living in darkness see a great light. Jesus brings that light to Galilee.
steps.question: Who do you know who is walking in darkness this Christmas?

steps.title: A light for every nation
steps.note: God's servant will bring salvation to the ends of the earth. Old Simeon holds the baby and praises God for this light.
steps.question: Why is it good news that Jesus came for every nation, not just one?

steps.title: Gifts for the king
steps.note: The psalm pictures kings from far away honoring Israel's king. The wise men worship the child and give their gifts.
steps.question: What could you give to Jesus this Christmas?

steps.title: Out of Egypt
steps.note: Hosea remembers God calling his son Israel out of Egypt. Matthew sees Jesus retracing Israel's story as the family returns from Egypt.
steps.question: How does Jesus living out Israel's story help us understand who he is?

name: The Lamb of God
summary: From a mountain in Genesis to the throne in Revelation, follow the Lamb who takes away sin.

steps.title: God will provide the lamb
steps.note: On the way up the mountain Abraham assures Isaac that God will provide the sacrifice. Centuries later John the Baptist points to Jesus and names Him as God’s Lamb.
steps.question: Why do you think God asked for a substitute instead of simply overlooking sin?

steps.title: The Passover
steps.note: In Egypt, households marked by a lamb’s blood were spared on the night of judgment. Paul identifies Christ as the Passover lamb, sacrificed for His people.
steps.question: What does it mean for you personally that judgment “passes over” because of Jesus?

steps.title: Without blemish
steps.note: The Passover lamb had to be without any defect. Peter says believers were bought back by the costly blood of Christ, the flawless Lamb.
steps.question: Why does it matter that Jesus was without fault?

steps.title: Led like a lamb
steps.note: Isaiah describes a suffering servant who goes silently to His death like a lamb. Philip meets an Ethiopian official reading this passage and explains that it is about Jesus.
steps.question: How did Philip use a single passage to explain the whole story of Jesus? Who could you do that for?

steps.title: The Lamb on the throne
steps.note: In his vision of heaven John sees a Lamb bearing the marks of sacrifice, standing at the center of the throne. The sacrifice has become the King.
steps.question: What changes when we see the one who was sacrificed now reigning?

steps.title: The light of the city
steps.note: Heaven praises the Lamb for redeeming people from every nation. In the new creation the city needs no sun, because the Lamb gives it light.
steps.question: How does the hope of the Lamb’s light shape the way you face dark seasons?

name: God with us
summary: The story of God making His home with people, from Eden to the New Jerusalem.

steps.title: Walking with God
steps.note: In Eden God was present with people in the garden. Sin broke that closeness. The Bible ends with the same hope restored, as God makes His home with humanity.
steps.question: What do you think was lost when people could no longer walk closely with God?

steps.title: The tabernacle
steps.note: God tells Moses to build a sanctuary so He can dwell among His people. When it is finished, His glory fills it.
steps.question: Why might God choose to live among a people who kept failing Him?

steps.title: The temple
steps.note: When Solomon dedicates the temple, the cloud of God’s glory fills it, just as it filled the tabernacle.
steps.question: What does the cloud of glory filling the temple tell us about what God wants?

steps.title: The Word became flesh
steps.note: John says the Word took on human life and lived among us, using a word that recalls the tabernacle tent, and that His glory was seen. Jesus is God’s presence in person.
steps.question: How does seeing Jesus as God’s presence in person change how you read the Gospels?

steps.title: The true temple
steps.note: Jesus calls His own body the temple. When He dies, the temple curtain tears from top to bottom, opening the way to God.
steps.question: What does the torn curtain mean for how you approach God in prayer?

steps.title: You are the temple
steps.note: Now God’s Spirit lives in His people. Together, and each one, believers are His temple.
steps.question: If God’s Spirit lives in you, how might that shape an ordinary Monday?

steps.title: No temple needed
steps.note: Ezekiel promised God would live among His people forever. John sees no temple building in the New Jerusalem, because God and the Lamb fill that role.
steps.question: What are you most looking forward to about living in God’s presence forever?

name: The promised King
summary: Promises of a King from Judah and the line of David, fulfilled in Jesus.

steps.title: The Lion of Judah
steps.note: Jacob’s blessing promises lasting royal rule to the tribe of Judah. In Revelation Jesus is honored as the victorious Lion from Judah.
steps.question: What kind of king did Israel expect, and how is Jesus similar or different?

steps.title: A throne forever
steps.note: God promises David a descendant whose kingdom will last forever. Gabriel tells Mary her son will receive the throne of His father David.
steps.question: Why does it matter that God kept His promise to David across a thousand years?

steps.title: A shoot from Jesse
steps.note: Isaiah sees new growth from the cut-down family line of Jesse, David’s father. Paul quotes this to show that the Messiah rules over the nations, who put their hope in Him.
steps.question: Where in your life does it feel like a “stump”, and what hope does this promise offer?

steps.title: Born in Bethlehem
steps.note: Micah names small Bethlehem as the birthplace of Israel’s coming ruler. When the wise men arrive looking for the King, the scholars point to Micah.
steps.question: Why do you think God chose a small town for the birth of the King?

steps.title: Riding on a donkey
steps.note: Zechariah pictures a humble King riding on a donkey. Jesus enters Jerusalem exactly this way.
steps.question: What does a king on a donkey teach us about how Jesus uses His power?

steps.title: Seated at the right hand
steps.note: In this psalm David hears God invite David’s own Lord to take the place of honor beside Him. At Pentecost Peter says this is about the risen and ascended Jesus.
steps.question: How does knowing Jesus reigns now affect the way you handle worry?

steps.title: A kingdom without end
steps.note: Daniel sees a figure like a son of man receive a kingdom that never ends. Revelation announces that the rule of the world now belongs to God and His Messiah forever.
steps.question: What would it look like to live today as a citizen of a kingdom that never ends?

name: The Spirit poured out
summary: The breath of God from creation to Pentecost and beyond.

steps.title: The breath of life
steps.note: God breathes life into the first human. After His resurrection Jesus breathes on His disciples and gives them the Holy Spirit. A new creation begins.
steps.question: What is the connection between God’s breath at creation and the Spirit Jesus gives?

steps.title: If only everyone had the Spirit
steps.note: Moses wishes all God’s people had the Spirit. Joel promises a day when God will pour out His Spirit on all people.
steps.question: Moses wished every believer had the Spirit. What difference would that make in your church?

steps.title: A new heart
steps.note: God promises to replace hearts of stone with hearts of flesh and to put His Spirit within. Paul says the Spirit now writes on human hearts, not on stone.
steps.question: Where do you need God to replace something hard with something new in you?

steps.title: Water for the thirsty
steps.note: God promises water on dry ground and His Spirit on His people. Jesus says rivers of living water will flow from those who believe, speaking of the Spirit.
steps.question: What are you thirsty for, and how does Jesus answer that thirst?

steps.title: Pentecost
steps.note: At Pentecost the Spirit comes on the disciples, and Peter explains that this is the outpouring Joel foretold.
steps.question: What surprised the crowd at Pentecost, and what might surprise people about your church?

steps.title: For every nation
steps.note: The Spirit comes on Gentiles at Cornelius' house. Joel’s promise for all people really does include everyone.
steps.question: Who might you overlook that God wants to include?

steps.title: Come and drink
steps.note: Isaiah invites the thirsty to drink without paying. The Bible closes with the Spirit and the Church repeating that invitation, offering the water of life as a free gift.
steps.question: Who could you invite this week to “come and drink”?

name: Eden to the new creation
summary: How the last pages of the Bible answer the first.

steps.title: Heaven and earth
steps.note: The Bible opens with God creating the heavens and the earth, and closes with a new heaven and a new earth.
steps.question: What do the first and last pages of the Bible tell us about God’s plan for the world?

steps.title: The first promise
steps.note: Right after the fall God promises that a descendant of the woman will defeat the serpent. Paul assures the church that God will soon bring Satan’s final defeat.
steps.question: Why is it significant that God promised rescue straight after the first sin?

steps.title: A blessing for all nations
steps.note: God promises Abraham that all nations will be blessed through him. Paul calls this the gospel announced in advance.
steps.question: How is the blessing promised to Abraham reaching people today?

steps.title: The way back
steps.note: Cherubim guard the way back to the tree of life. Hebrews says Jesus has opened a new way into God’s presence.
steps.question: What does it mean that the way back to God is now open?

steps.title: No more curse
steps.note: The ground comes under a curse because of sin. In the new creation the curse is gone for good.
steps.question: Which part of the world’s brokenness are you most longing to see healed?

steps.title: The tree of life
steps.note: The tree of life stood in Eden. It returns in the New Jerusalem, with leaves for the healing of the nations.
steps.question: What do the leaves “for the healing of the nations” suggest about the future?

steps.title: Face to face
steps.note: After sinning, Adam and Eve hid from God. At the end of the story His people see Him face to face.
steps.question: How does the hope of seeing God face to face change the way you live now?

name: God’s covenant promises
summary: Follow the binding promises God makes, from Noah to the new covenant in Jesus.

steps.title: A promise after the flood
steps.note: After the flood God binds Himself never again to destroy the earth by water. Isaiah points back to that promise to assure exiles that God’s kindness will not be withdrawn.
steps.question: Why do you think God chooses to bind Himself with promises?

steps.title: Abraham’s family
steps.note: God promises to be the God of Abraham and his descendants forever. Paul says everyone who belongs to Christ is counted as Abraham’s family and shares that promise.
steps.question: What does it mean to you to be part of a family of faith that spans thousands of years?

steps.title: Blood of the covenant
steps.note: At Sinai Moses seals the covenant with sacrificial blood. At the Last Supper Jesus speaks of His own blood as the blood of the covenant, poured out for forgiveness.
steps.question: How does communion take on new meaning in light of this connection?

steps.title: A promise to David
steps.note: God promises David a throne that will last forever. Psalm 89 holds God to that covenant even when the kingdom seems to be failing.
steps.question: How do you hold on to God’s promises when circumstances seem to say the opposite?

steps.title: The new covenant
steps.note: Jeremiah looks ahead to a new covenant written on hearts. Jesus announces that the new covenant begins with His death.
steps.question: What is the difference between rules written on stone and a law written on the heart?

steps.title: An everlasting covenant
steps.note: Ezekiel promises a covenant of peace that lasts forever. Hebrews closes by naming Jesus as the shepherd raised to life through the blood of that eternal covenant.
steps.question: Where do you most need the peace this covenant promises?

name: Out of Egypt: the road to freedom
summary: The rescue from slavery becomes the pattern for the greater freedom Jesus brings.

steps.title: God sees and hears
steps.note: At the burning bush God tells Moses He has seen His people’s suffering and come to rescue them. Stephen retells this moment to show that God has always acted to save.
steps.question: What does it mean to you that God sees and hears suffering?

steps.title: Through the sea
steps.note: God opens a path through the sea for Israel to escape. Paul looks back on this crossing as a lesson and a picture for believers.
steps.question: When has God made a way for you where there seemed to be none?

steps.title: Bread from heaven
steps.note: God feeds Israel with manna in the desert. Jesus says the Father now gives the true bread from heaven, which is Jesus Himself.
steps.question: What are you relying on to sustain you, and how does Jesus offer something deeper?

steps.title: Water from the rock
steps.note: Water flows from a rock to save a thirsty people. Paul says that rock pointed to Christ.
steps.question: How has Jesus provided for you in a dry season?

steps.title: Called out of Egypt
steps.note: Hosea remembers God calling Israel, His son, out of Egypt. Matthew sees the same pattern when the young Jesus returns from Egypt.
steps.question: Why might Matthew want readers to see Jesus as reliving Israel’s story?

steps.title: Freed to be free
steps.note: The commandments begin by reminding Israel that God freed them from slavery. Paul urges believers to stand firm in the freedom Christ has won and not return to slavery.
steps.question: What old patterns try to pull you back, and what helps you stay free?

steps.title: The song of the rescued
steps.note: After crossing the sea Moses and Israel sing of God’s victory. In Revelation the redeemed sing the song of Moses and the Lamb.
steps.question: What rescue in your life is worth singing about?

name: Our great High Priest
summary: Priests stood between God and the people. Hebrews shows how Jesus fulfils that role for good.

steps.title: A mysterious priest
steps.note: Abraham meets Melchizedek, a king and priest who blesses him. Hebrews uses this brief scene to explain a priesthood older and greater than Aaron’s.
steps.question: Why might Hebrews look so far back to explain who Jesus is?

steps.title: A priest forever
steps.note: Psalm 110 speaks of a king who is also a priest forever. Hebrews applies it directly to Jesus.
steps.question: What difference does it make that Jesus’ priesthood never ends?

steps.title: Carrying the people’s names
steps.note: Aaron carried the names of Israel’s tribes over his heart into God’s presence. Hebrews says Jesus always lives to speak to the Father on behalf of His people.
steps.question: How does it feel to know Jesus is praying for you?

steps.title: The Day of Atonement
steps.note: Once a year the high priest brought sacrificial blood into the Most Holy Place. Jesus entered once for all with His own blood and secured lasting redemption.
steps.question: What does “once for all” mean for the guilt you still carry?

steps.title: Confidence to come near
steps.note: Even the high priest could not enter the holiest place whenever he chose. Hebrews says believers can now approach God with confidence because of Jesus.
steps.question: What holds you back from coming near to God, and how does this answer it?

steps.title: A kingdom of priests
steps.note: At Sinai God calls Israel to be a kingdom of priests. Peter gives the same calling to the church, to declare God’s goodness to the world.
steps.question: How could you serve as a bridge between God and the people around you this week?

name: Water and new life
summary: From creation to the river of life, water carries the story of cleansing, rescue and renewal.

steps.title: Spirit and water
steps.note: At creation the Spirit moves over the waters. Jesus tells Nicodemus that entering God’s kingdom requires being born of water and the Spirit.
steps.question: What does it mean to be made new rather than just improved?

steps.title: Saved through the flood
steps.note: Noah’s family is carried safely through the waters of judgment. Peter links this rescue to baptism and the new life it signifies.
steps.question: What does your baptism, or the idea of baptism, say about where your safety lies?

steps.title: Through the sea
steps.note: Israel passes through the sea on dry ground. Paul describes the crossing as a kind of baptism into a new identity.
steps.question: What did God bring you out of, and what did He bring you into?

steps.title: The spring of living water
steps.note: Jeremiah says God’s people abandoned Him, the source of living water, for broken cisterns. Jesus offers a Samaritan woman living water that only He can give.
steps.question: What “broken cisterns” are tempting to rely on today?

steps.title: Led to springs
steps.note: The Shepherd of Psalm 23 leads His sheep beside quiet waters. In Revelation the Lamb shepherds His people to springs of living water and wipes away their tears.
steps.question: Where do you need the Shepherd to lead you to rest?

steps.title: The river of life
steps.note: Ezekiel sees a river flowing from the temple that brings life wherever it goes. John sees the river of the water of life flowing from God’s throne in the new creation.
steps.question: How could your life be a channel for God’s life to reach others?

name: God keeps His promises
summary: For kids: God always does what He says.

steps.title: The rainbow
steps.note: After the flood God put a rainbow in the sky as a sign of His promise. In heaven, John sees a rainbow all around God’s throne.
steps.question: What does a rainbow remind you about God?

steps.title: Count the stars
steps.note: God told Abraham to look at the stars and promised him a family that big. Hebrews says it really happened!
steps.question: Can you think of a promise someone kept for you?

steps.title: A baby for Sarah
steps.note: Sarah was very old, but God gave her a baby boy just like He promised.
steps.question: Is anything too hard for God?

steps.title: Every promise
steps.note: Joshua said not one of God’s good promises failed. Paul says every promise of God is a yes in Jesus.
steps.question: Which promise of God would you like to remember this week?

name: Jesus, the Good Shepherd
summary: For kids: Jesus looks after His sheep.

steps.title: My shepherd
steps.note: David said the Lord is his shepherd. Jesus said, I am the good shepherd.
steps.question: What does a shepherd do for the sheep?

steps.title: The lost sheep
steps.note: God said He would go looking for His lost sheep. Jesus told a story about a shepherd who searched until he found the one that was lost.
steps.question: How do you think the lost sheep felt when it was found?

steps.title: Carried close
steps.note: Isaiah says God carries the little lambs close to His heart. Jesus took the children in His arms and blessed them.
steps.question: How does it feel to know Jesus loves children?

steps.title: Following the shepherd
steps.note: Jesus’ sheep know His voice and follow Him. One day He will lead them to fresh water and wipe away every tear.
steps.question: How can we listen to Jesus?

name: God’s big rescues
summary: For kids: stories of God saving His people.

steps.title: Noah’s ark
steps.note: God told Noah to build a big boat, and it kept his family safe in the flood.
steps.question: What would you take on Noah’s ark?

steps.title: The lions’ den
steps.note: God sent an angel to shut the lions’ mouths so Daniel was safe. Hebrews remembers people who trusted God like that.
steps.question: When do you need to be brave?

steps.title: Jonah and the big fish
steps.note: Jonah prayed inside the fish, and God rescued him. Jesus said His own rescue would be like Jonah’s three days.
steps.question: Where could you pray to God? (Anywhere!)

steps.title: The greatest rescue
steps.note: God promised to look for the lost. Jesus said He came to find and save people who are lost.
steps.question: Who is someone you could tell about Jesus?

name: The first Christmas
summary: For kids: God kept his promises when Jesus was born.

steps.title: Born in Bethlehem
steps.note: Long before Jesus was born, God said a special king would come from little Bethlehem. And that is just where Jesus was born!
steps.question: Why do you think God picked a small town?

steps.title: God with us
steps.note: God promised a baby called Immanuel, which means God with us. Jesus is God who came to be with us.
steps.question: How does it feel to know God is always with you?

steps.title: Follow the star
steps.note: God said a star would come from Jacob's family. Wise men saw a star and followed it all the way to Jesus.
steps.question: If you could bring a gift to baby Jesus, what would it be?

steps.title: A baby who is King
steps.note: God promised a child who would be a king of peace. Angels told shepherds that this Savior had been born!
steps.question: Who can you tell the good news to this Christmas?
